answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity expensive. Each agent must lock real collateral before it can attest or earn reputation, and that stake is slashed when its claims prove false. A thousand fake agents would need a thousand separate bonds, so attacker cost scales linearly with identity count while an honest agent pays once. Reputation grows on a trellis of verified counterparties, so new identities start at zero, and a periodic pulse re-checks every seat against its locked basalt-hard stake, dropping those that thinned it.
